entries.claim: This AC1 end-to-end test is self-defeating: it keeps the ingest lock held for the rest of the run, but the hooks it invokes are described as spawning detached ingest work that exits without writing when that lock is busy. That means the later assertions over `injection/` and `decisions/` cannot be satisfied by the sequence as written.
entries.failure_scenario: With the lock held, `hook SessionStart` and `hook UserPromptSubmit` do not create the scratch files the test later stats, so the run fails on missing paths before it can prove their modes or ctimes.

counter_evidence.note: crates/verbatim/src/cmd/hook.rs:198-207 (`run`): the detached `ingest` spawn and the injection arm are separate; `inject(event, payload)` runs on the hook process own thread (hook.rs:242-258) and its doc at hook.rs:222-227 states nothing on that thread takes the ingest lock. The files the test stats are written by that arm, not by the ingest: `state.save` at crates/verbatim-core/src/inject/brief.rs:104 and :126 writes `injection/`, and `decision.save` at crates/verbatim-core/src/inject/prompt.rs:212 writes `decisions/` (create_dir_all + tmp/rename at decision.rs:278-306). A held ingest lock only makes the detached ingest exit without draining, which is exactly why PLAN-3 Task 3 holds it: it keeps the decisions file on disk long enough to stat.
